# Gravity and energy {#sec-ch06}

Gravity does work on the flow, and a finite-volume code has to decide where to book it. This chapter is about
that decision and what each answer costs. It covers the cell form, which applies the body force and the work
$\rho v_1g_1$ in the same cell; the face form, which books the work as a flux difference of potential energy
across the cell's $x_1$ faces; the global fixer that repairs the cell form's budget once per step; the
corrected-PE face work, which makes the booked work fourth-order consistent with the scheme's own mass fluxes;
the gravity work inside the vertical implicit operator; and a closing comparison of what each form conserves and
which diagnostic measures it. The thread running through all of them is a single identity, @eq-ch06-dwork-booked:
choose a discrete potential energy, and the work that conserves total energy plus that potential energy is
determined. Every form in this chapter is that identity with a different choice of $P$, and the differences
between the forms are differences in how accurate $P$ is, not in how the work is applied. The momentum equation
is untouched throughout; only the energy row changes. The hydrostatic reference state these forms are often used
with is @sec-ch05, and the implicit solver they couple into is the vertical implicit solve, which the
time-integration chapter covers.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-deps
#| fig-cap: "Dependency map of the gravity and energy schemes. Nodes are the schemes of this chapter; a solid arrow reads 'requires', a dashed arrow 'implies', and a vermillion arrow with a bar head 'turns off'. The corrected-PE face work requires the face form, implies the $E+P$ invariant in place of $E+\\mathrm{PE}_d$, and turns off the cp3/cp5/weno5 curvature flux; the fixer requires the cell form and is refused with either face form. Read it with the switch coverage matrix, which lists which combinations a test actually exercises."
#| fig-alt: "Directed graph of six nodes labelled cell form, face form, face-wallc, gravity-work fixer, corrected-PE face work and VIC gravity work, with solid, dashed and barred arrows between them."
#| echo: false

```

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cell form | `gravity-work: cell` | on | 1 | `test_forcing` |
| Face form | `gravity-work: face` | off | 2 | `test_horizontal_flux_covariance` |
| Wall-cell face form | `gravity-work: face-wallc` | off | 1 at walls | `test_gravity_work_fixer` |
| Gravity-work fixer | `gravity-work-fixer` | on with `cell` | global | `test_gravity_work_fixer` |
| Corrected-PE face work (@sec-ch06-dwork) | `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` | on with `face` | 4 | `test_gravity_work_radial_exact` |
| VIC gravity work | `implicit-scheme` $\neq0$ | off | linearised | `test_implicit_face_work_operator` |

: The schemes of this chapter, their switches and defaults, the order of the booked gravity work, and the test
that carries each one. Orders are of the booked work against the exact work of the scheme's own $x_1$ mass
fluxes; "global" means the fixer corrects the domain integral, not the local error. Full ctest names and their
tolerances are in each scheme's Tests layer. {#tbl-ch06-schemes}
